destination.name: Hay
destination.tagline: A Sturt Highway town of shearing, a gaol museum and wartime internment history.
destination.description: Hay is a small town on the Murrumbidgee River on the Sturt Highway, in flat western Riverina country. Its three visitor stops are ShearOutback, which hosts the Australian Shearers' Hall of Fame and live shearing demonstrations, the 1878 Hay Gaol museum and the Dunera Museum in the railway station. The Dunera museum covers the 1,984 Dunera Boys and the internees held at Hay between 1940 and 1946.
whyVisit: Explore Hay Gaol's windmills and bark canoe

goodToKnow.title: Shearing times
goodToKnow.detail: ShearOutback runs live shearing demonstrations at 10:30 am and 1:00 pm daily; entry is about $20.

goodToKnow.title: Bring a car
goodToKnow.detail: There is no car hire in Hay, and the town is reached by the Sturt Highway, so arrive with your own vehicle.

goodToKnow.title: Summer heat
goodToKnow.detail: Summers regularly pass 40 °C and the record is 47.7 °C, so do your walking in the morning or outside summer.

destination.bestTimeBlurb: {months} sit between summers that regularly pass 40 °C and winter days that can stay under 10 °C.
